basic_info.name: Marek Health
basic_info.category: Cash-pay concierge telehealth platform for health optimization (hormone replacement/TRT, peptide protocols, GLP-1 weight loss, diagnostic lab sales via sister brand Marek Diagnostics). Not a lab, not an AI interpreter — a coaching-led telehealth clinic.
basic_info.country: United States (US residents only, 18+; Marek Diagnostics cannot serve NY, NJ, RI; one third-party review lists HI as also excluded)
basic_info.stage: Growth-stage private company. Founded 2020 (CB Insights; some sources say 2019), based in Pontiac, Michigan. Claims 50,000+ clients transformed. No acquisition or bankruptcy signals; active site with 2026 copyright, growing Trustpilot volume.
basic_info.pricing_model: No flat subscription — itemized pay-per-service with cancel anytime (explicit anti-subscription positioning: 'we don't offer any set subscription plans'). Current price ladder (site + third parties, 2025-2026): Intake bundle $299 (coach intake call + custom lab report + 25-min licensed-provider consult; third-party reviews cite an older $250 price) with a MANDATORY minimum $450 lab panel purchase to unlock discounted lab pricing. Base hormone/TRT protocol $225-$275/month medication cost ('starts at $225/mo', TRT Picks June 2026). All-in annual cost for TRT with required labs ~$2,500-$5,400/year (independent estimates). GLP-1: compounded semaglutide ~$250-$400/mo, tirzepatide ~$350-$500/mo. Peptides e.g. BPC-157 15mg ~$350/vial. Enclomiphene ~$75/mo. Lab panels at Marek Diagnostics: from ~$150-$350 (65+ biomarkers) to $595 Comprehensive (80+) to ~$700-$1,950 Complete/Executive tiers; genetics $200-$500. Follow-up check-in sessions $100-$150 each, minimum ~2/year. No insurance accepted; FSA/HSA accepted via TrueMed. Recent changes: intake price raised $250 -> $299; user reports (Aug 2025) claim panels now contain fewer markers at higher prices [uncertain].
basic_info.target_user: Biohackers, men 35+ with low-T/performance goals (primary), competitive and recreational fitness community (MPMD audience: bodybuilding, UFC, jiu-jitsu fans), plus a secondary women's health cohort (postpartum thyroid/HRT cases visible in testimonials). Explicitly NOT for price-sensitive users or people wanting a single cheap prescription.
basic_info.scale_metrics: Claims 50,000+ clients (self-reported, site hero). Trustpilot 4.9/5 with ~773 reviews (Nov 2025 crawl; third-party reviews Mar-Jun 2026 cite 4.8-4.9 from 880+ — volume growing, so the count is a moving number; the 4.8 cited in the research brief has since ticked to 4.9). Estimated revenue ~$18.7M (Compworth estimate) / $10-25M band (LeadIQ); 50-200 employees. LinkedIn ~3,100 followers. No VC funding rounds found on Crunchbase — appears bootstrapped/founder-owned [uncertain]. Durable-trait read: revenue concentrated in a niche audience funneled from the More Plates More Dates YouTube channel; defensible while the content flywheel runs, but the moat is audience + coach relationships, not tech.

product.core_features: Guided Optimization(R) program: (1) personalized lab panel curated by a health coach (100+ biomarkers available); (2) custom lab analysis report with actionable recommendations; (3) 25-minute consult with a licensed medical provider (MD/DO via partnered medical group); (4) customized protocol — prescriptions (testosterone injections/cream, thyroid, enclomiphene, HCG, nandrolone, oxandrolone, semaglutide/tirzepatide, peptides: BPC-157, TB-4, CJC-1295/Ipamorelin, PT-141, Sermorelin, GHK-Cu) + targeted supplements from their own dispensary; (5) meds shipped to door from FDA-approved/compounding pharmacies; (6) monthly coach check-ins, refills, follow-up labs every 6 months (mandatory), provider visits every 6 months, annual physical required. Sister brand Marek Diagnostics sells standalone lab panels (a la carte, no coaching needed). Treatment verticals marketed by goal: testosterone, weight loss, hair loss, sexual health, sleep, cognition ('think sharper'), heart health, fertility, skin/looks.
product.signature_differentiator: The coach-as-retention-engine model applied to lab data: every client gets a named human health coach (not a doctor, not an algorithm) who interprets labs against 'optimal' ranges rather than disease reference ranges, builds the protocol, and maintains a parasocial relationship via monthly check-ins and fast email replies — Trustpilot reviews overwhelmingly praise coaches BY NAME (Sawyer, Mars, Bryan, Joshua). Combined with: (a) the deepest biomarker menu in consumer telehealth (65-100+ markers vs 15-30 at TRT competitors); (b) the widest catalog under one roof (TRT + peptides + GLP-1 + thyroid + fertility); (c) a content-flywheel founder (Derek/MPMD, millions of YouTube views) plus athlete endorsement wall (Samson Dauda, Sean Brady, Derek Lunsford, Craig Jones). Nobody else bundles 'influencer trust + concierge coach + full optimization pharmacy + own lab storefront'. The interpretation itself is deliberately human and premium — that is the moat they chose, opposite of AI-first players.
product.lab_data_handling: Labs are the entry product and the recurring heartbeat. Entry: coach curates a custom panel during intake; mandatory minimum $450 panel purchase. Collection: blood draw at 2,000+ Quest Diagnostics partner sites (order form emailed; some third-party reviews also mention at-home draw/kits as an option [uncertain]). Turnaround: results typically within 14 business days; users report up to 3 weeks. Marek Diagnostics sells standalone panels (Total Health tiers: Comprehensive $595/80+ markers, Complete ~$700/100 markers, Executive ~$1,950 [uncertain]; budget panels from ~$150; build-your-own from 100+ individual biomarkers; genetics: APOE $200, MTHFR $225, CAG-repeat androgen-receptor $500). They accept externally-drawn labs if less than 3 months old at application. Cadence is contractual: re-test at least every 6 months to stay a client, provider visit every 6 months, physical exam every 12 months — the retest loop is the recurring-revenue engine. No CGM program, no wearable integration, no at-home chip; blood-only.
product.family_dependents_depth: None. 18+ only, single-user accounts, US-only. No dependent profiles, no caregiver mode, no pediatric reference ranges, no hereditary-risk module. The founder's origin quote ('difficult to get medical oversight for myself and my family') gestures at family motivation, but the product is strictly individual. Whole gap left open — nothing in their funnel addresses children's labs, spouse dashboards, or inherited-risk flagging (their only genetics are performance/APOE consumer tests, not family risk assessment).
product.doctor_sharing: No external-physician sharing features (no export brief, no PDF summary for your PCP, no SOAP/consultation handoff marketed). The 'doctor' in the loop is their own partnered provider who prescribes after the intake; the platform explicitly disclaims being a clinic ('Marek Health is not a healthcare clinic... a platform that connects clients with healthcare providers'). Patients can request invoices/lab requisitions for FSA/HSA, but no CPT/ICD-10 codes are provided (no insurance billing), which actively complicates sharing results back into the insured-care system.
product.action_loop_monetization: The single best live example of 'the margin migrated to the action loop'. Sequence: cheap-feeling entry ($299 intake) gated by $450 minimum labs -> human interpretation creates anxiety + aspiration ('optimal ranges', not normal ranges) -> protocol = recurring monthly meds at markup (base $225-275/mo, compounded in their pharmacy network; peptides ~$350/vial at 2-3x grey-market price; GLP-1 $250-500/mo) -> supplement dispensary upsell (coaches reportedly on commission pushing high-markup OTC supplements, per Muscle & Brawn review) -> mandatory 6-month retest + $100-150 check-ins keep the loop billing -> cancellation friction is soft (cancel anytime) because emotional anchoring to the named coach + visible biomarker improvement does the retention, not contracts. Annual value extracted per engaged TRT client: ~$2,500-$5,400. Key structural lessons: (1) they sell the interpretation as a relationship, not a report; (2) the lab is the razor, protocol+pharmacy is the blade; (3) 'no subscription' framing is a trust hack while actual behavior is subscription-like recurring spend; (4) Trustpilot is farmed as a channel (company replies to 100% of reviews, requests testimonials) feeding the funnel; (5) the content influencer (MPMD) supplies warm traffic at zero CAC.

technology.ai_approach: No AI claims anywhere. Interpretation is fully human: health coaches (background/training not disclosed; some reviews note 'limited training' for coaches [uncertain]) produce the custom report; licensed MD/DO partnered providers make prescribing decisions. No LLM, no proprietary engine, no published accuracy methodology, no clinical-decision-support claims. Their 'technology' is operational: booking, portal, e-commerce, pharmacy logistics.
technology.data_inputs: Blood labs (65-100+ biomarkers per panel; 100+ individual markers available a la carte), intake questionnaire/symptoms + goals, health history, physical exam documentation, consumer genetics tests (APOE, MTHFR, CAG repeat). No wearable data, no CGM, no continuous monitoring, no dietary/photo inputs found.
technology.data_interoperability: Minimal. Ingestion: their own Quest-based lab orders; they accept external lab results (PDF/paper) less than 3 months old at application. Exhaust: results delivered via email and client portal; invoices/requisitions on request; no FHIR, no Apple Health Records, no Health Connect, no LIS integrations, no public API, no WhatsApp channel. The portal is a walled garden by design — data stays inside the monetization loop.
technology.platform: Web only (Next.js marketing site + client portal for booking/results/orders). No native mobile app found in app stores or linked from the site [uncertain — none surfaced]. Support via email, SMS notifications, phone during business hours (Mon-Fri 9-5 EST).

ux.onboarding: Sign-up wizard (state -> DOB -> name -> phone/email/password -> telehealth consent) -> book intake with a coach -> coach builds custom panel -> draw at Quest -> wait up to 14 business days for results -> custom report -> 25-min provider consult -> protocol shipped. Time-to-value: 3-5 weeks realistically (plus 1-2 week wait for intake during busy periods). Friction-heavy and intentionally high-commitment ($299 + $450 labs before any treatment) — a filter that self-selects high-intent, high-LTV clients and repels bargain hunters by design.
ux.data_visualization: Client portal shows lab results against their 'optimal range' framing (founders' marketing rails against 'arbitrary' disease reference ranges). No evidence of trend charts over time, dashboards, scores, or longitudinal visualization in public materials — visualization is not their selling point; the coach narrating your numbers is. Specific portal visuals unverifiable without an account [uncertain].
ux.engagement_channel: Retention = named human coach with monthly check-ins + fast async email replies (the single most-praised thing across hundreds of reviews), SMS reminders, refill logistics, and the 6-month mandatory retest cycle that re-opens the protocol conversation twice a year. Around the product: MPMD YouTube/podcast ecosystem (education-as-marketing), newsletter, Instagram/YouTube, athlete endorsement wall, testimonial carousel, Trustpilot review-reply flywheel. No streaks, no gamification, no community forum, no WhatsApp, no push-notification app — engagement is parasocial and human, not mechanic.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: No published accuracy metrics, no clinical studies, no peer-reviewed methodology — trust is built on LegitScript certification, MD/DO prescribers, FDA-approved pharmacy claims, named-coach accountability, and a 4.9/5 Trustpilot (773-880+ reviews, ~97% five-star, all labeled 'Unprompted'). Caveats a credibility audit should flag: (1) coaches are not clinicians and their training is undisclosed, yet they design protocols and sell supplements on (reportedly) commission — inherent conflict of interest; (2) reviews are coach-personal (parasocial) rather than outcome-verified; company replies to every review and solicits testimonials, and reviews.io-style incentive bias cannot be excluded; (3) 'optimal ranges' framing is marketing, not evidence-based thresholds; (4) one 2025 user report claims panels shrank while prices rose; (5) Schedule III anabolic prescribing (nandrolone, oxandrolone) under a 'optimization' wrapper is ethically contested. Billing transparency: prices NOT public pre-signup for meds/protocols (intake and labs are the only public prices) — you learn protocol cost after the paid intake.
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Operates the standard US telehealth corporate-practice-of-medicine split: 'Marek Health is not a healthcare clinic... does not administer healthcare nor prescribe' — it is a platform connecting clients to partnered licensed providers who prescribe; LegitScript-certified website; telehealth informed consent mandatory at signup; Schedule III controlled substances handled through licensed providers; compounds (semaglutide/tirzepatide, peptides) via compounding pharmacies in the FDA enforcement-gray zone (no FDA evaluation of compounded formulations; peptide clinical claims unverified — classic wellness-vs-device line walked by never claiming to diagnose or treat disease, only to 'optimize'). Cash-pay elective positioning avoids insurance fraud surface entirely (no CPT/ICD-10 codes issued). No FDA SaMD exposure because there is no software-as-device claim — the lesson for a Brazilian SaMD context (ANVISA RDC 657/2022): Marek keeps every claim in the 'optimization/wellness + licensed prescriber' lane and never lets software interpret or decide alone; a Brazilian AI-interpretation app cannot copy this wholesale because interpretation-of-results claims themselves are what ANVISA regulates, but the 'human prescriber owns the decision, software never diagnoses' architecture is the transferable compliance pattern.
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What they DO NOT do (= Dr. Exame openings): (1) no family/dependents/caregiver mode, no pediatric ranges, no hereditary-risk layer — the exact pillar the brief says no US player covers well; (2) no instant/free self-serve interpretation — first value arrives weeks later behind a $749 paywall ($299 + $450 labs); (3) no upload-your-own-PDF-labs-for-immediate-reading product (labs must be theirs or <3 months old external); (4) no trends/longitudinal visualization emphasis, no scores; (5) no wearable/CGM/Health-Connect ingestion; (6) no WhatsApp-channel engagement (irrelevant in US, decisive in Brazil); (7) US-only — LatAm/PT-BR market untouched; (8) no B2B/employer or lab-partner distribution. What WORKS (inspiration, not copy): the action-loop economics (interpretation is the funnel, protocol+pharmacy+retest is the profit); named-human-coach trust engine farmed into public reviews; itemized 'no-subscription' framing that still behaves like recurring revenue; mandatory 6-month retest as contractual retention; niche-content founder funnel with zero CAC; premium 'optimal vs normal ranges' narrative that justifies 2-3x pricing; gating entry with a minimum lab purchase to qualify buyers.
trust_gaps.relevance: High. Marek Health is the canonical proof of the thesis in this research (monetization lives in the action-loop after interpretation, not in the reading itself) and the benchmark for coach-led premium monetization, Trustpilot-as-channel, and retest-cycle retention. It is not a tech competitor — no AI, no app, no family layer, no Brazil presence — so relevance is strategic/monetization rather than feature-parity.
